_source: MMG_v19_Client_Manual_Testing_Guideline_FG05-FG14_v1.0.xlsx / Testing Guideline, rows 44-46 (TC-CHN-001, TC-CHN-005, TC-CHN-011). Scope of this pass: those three cases only — the remaining ten FG-08 rows of the older MMG_v19_Test_Cases_Grouped_by_Feature_v3.0.xlsx are untouched and stay NOT_IMPLEMENTED.
_target: Odoo 19 only. The workbook navigates 'E-commerce Connectors > Configuration > Store Configuration > Manage Stores' — a menu level that exists only in the v19 port (omni_manage_channel/views/ecommerce_channel_views.xml:76-77; v15 hung Manage Stores straight off Configuration at novobi-omni-addons/omni_manage_channel/views/ecommerce_channel_views.xml:82) — and its Overview expectations describe the rebuilt v19 dashboard. Every test calls require_v19 first and reports BLOCKED on anything else.
_modules: omni_manage_channel 19.0.1.1.0, multichannel_order 19.0.1.0.0, multichannel_product 19.0.1.2.0, multichannel_fulfillment 19.0.1.0.0 and multichannel_shopify 19.0.1.1.0, branch staging_19. require_connector() probes one field per module (status / auto_create_master_product / is_enable_inventory_sync / kanban_dashboard_period / shopify_hostname) and reports BLOCKED naming the missing ones, because FG-08's expectations span all five.
_policy: All three cases are implemented for real, with no blocked stubs. FG-08's earlier wip/fg08 pass blocked TC-CHN-001 on the grounds that the QA clone's channel instances were inactive; that is no longer the situation — the v19 restore carries one ACTIVE Shopify store — and none of these three cases needs the store to be contacted, so all three run.
_read_only_by_construction: Every RPC call goes through tests/fg08/common.py::ReadOnlyRPC, which delegates only search/search_read/search_count/read/read_group/fields_get/get_view/get_views/name_search/has_group/web_search_read/web_read/context_get plus get_dashboard_datas and get_graph_datas on ecommerce.channel, and raises ReadOnlyViolation for anything else. This is not belt-and-braces: the single ecommerce.channel row on the v19 restore is the LIVE Medicine Man Gallery store (active=True, auto_import_data=True, environment='production', a real access token in the channel secret store), and several public methods on it reach Shopify — check_connection/button_check_connection/reconnect via _shopify_check_connection -> shopify_api.shop.all() (multichannel_shopify/models/ecommerce_channel.py:123-138), shopify_refresh_location (:306), bulk_inventory_sync, the Auto Import buttons, and write() itself for a shopify channel whenever a credential field is in vals (:427-435, 445-451). TC-CHN-001 step 8 forbids pressing those buttons; the guard makes the property checkable by reading one class instead of auditing three test files, and TEST-FG08-CHN-001 asserts it by attempting write/reconnect/shopify_refresh_location/enable_auto_import_data and requiring all four to be refused before reaching Odoo.
_no_baseline_in_hand: TC-CHN-001 and TC-CHN-005 are comparison cases against a Novobi printout of the old system. The platform does not hold that printout and there is no v15 database on this workstation to generate one from (mmg_15 is an empty skeleton, so framework.fg_common.reconcile would report BLOCKED for want of a baseline). The suite therefore does the half it can do properly: it captures the complete machine-readable inventory of every value the workbook asks the tester to compare into CSV artifacts, asserts every invariant that does not need the printout, and prints what is left as RESIDUAL MANUAL STEP. No expected-result line is silently dropped.
_no_cross_test_fixtures: The workbook chains the cases (TC-CHN-005's and TC-CHN-011's preconditions are both 'TC-CHN-001 has passed'). AUTOMATION_CONVENTIONS rule 5 forbids depending on another test's state, so each test resolves the store itself through the screen's own action domain and context rather than a captured id. The registry order values 800/801/802 still reproduce the workbook's Order of Testing sequence — step 2.0 (TC-CHN-001, TC-CHN-005, behind GATE 2) then step 6.0 (TC-CHN-011, behind GATE 6).
_no_browser: All three cases are DATA or API; no Playwright instance is launched, so a full FG-08 run is light on the machine. The consequence is stated rather than hidden: this suite does not prove that the OWL components paint. It asserts the arch the browser is handed (get_view returns the assembled, inheritance-merged architecture) and the payload it is handed (get_dashboard_datas / get_graph_datas are the same public methods the card's computes call), which is everything the render displays. The render itself is covered by the module's own browser_js test, omni_manage_channel/tests/test_dashboard_ui.py, which runs in the Odoo test runner rather than this platform (docs/CURRENT_ARCHITECTURE.md section 8).

TC-CHN-001.reason: The four-tab field-by-field review. Four things are asserted without the printout: (1) the three notebook tabs exist with the exact strings the workbook names, in its order — which is decided by view priority across three different modules (multichannel_product 40, multichannel_fulfillment 50, multichannel_order 1000), so a re-prioritised inherit would reorder the tester's screen and is caught; (2) every one of the 36 fields the workbook's steps 2-7 names is on the tab it says, resolved against the ASSEMBLED arch, which matters because five of them are placed by multichannel_shopify through xpaths into groups that other modules own; (3) the two things the workbook warns about on a saved store — Name readonly='write_date != False' and Platform invisible='write_date != False' — and that Access Token carries password='1' and is not empty, read without the value ever entering a log or a CSV; (4) the two failure shapes its If It Fails column names, neither of which needs a baseline: a configured many2one pointing at an archived or deleted record (the 'reverted to a default … will silently mis-route real orders' shape, checked over 18 routing fields), and a sub-table that the module's own constraints require to be non-empty but which came across empty (the 'a LIST with fewer rows … means rules were lost' shape, checked against check_active_warehouses, check_mapping_locations, and the required= bindings behind Auto Override and Export from Master). The printout comparison itself is a RESIDUAL MANUAL STEP served by TC-CHN-001-store-settings-inventory.csv (tab, workbook label, technical field, type, resolved display value, row count, whether it is on screen) and a row-counts-only companion, both written from a finally block so they exist when an assertion failed. The suite also briefs the tester on what is legitimately gone or renamed since v15 — the four deliberately dropped fields (oauth_version, state, is_in_syncing, last_option_sync_product) are asserted to be still gone, and default_payment_method_id -> default_payment_method_line_id and payment.method.mapping.payment_method_id -> payment_method_line_id are recorded — so a printout comparison does not report them as losses. Expected to FAIL on the current build; see _finding_salesperson.
TC-CHN-001.expected_verdict: FAILED on the Salesperson assertion (workbook Expected Result line 4). Every other assertion is expected to pass on the v19 restore.
residual_manual: Tick every row of TC-CHN-001-store-settings-inventory.csv off against the Novobi printout — only the printout says what each value should be.
Compare TC-CHN-001-list-row-counts.csv first: a short list means rules were lost, which is the more serious of the two shapes the workbook names.
Tick Hostname off against the printout (the value is in the log).
On a single-company database the Company field is not rendered at all (groups='base.group_multi_company'); tick it off from the log instead.

TC-CHN-005.reason: The two values and the filter. Status is asserted to be ecommerce.channel.status — a non-stored Selection computed from nothing but active (_get_status, omni_manage_channel/models/ecommerce_channel.py:311-313, byte-identical to v15's :222-224) — so reading it cannot probe the store, and the reading is asserted to agree with active, which turns a stale value into a failure rather than a mystery. The suite also warns the tester off is_sync, a different Selection on the same model labelled 'Sync Data' (:78) that is NULL on the restore and is not what the list binds. Last Order Sync is asserted non-blank and not today's date against the SERVER's clock rather than the workstation's, read from the current user's login_date — which the web session this platform opens has just stamped via _update_last_login (odoo/addons/base/models/res_users.py:233, 742-746, 775) — because the field carries default=fields.Datetime.now (:83) and is re-stamped to now by reconnect() (:325-337) and enable_auto_import_data() (:597-603), so a fresh-looking value means something re-stamped it. 'Clear the Connected filter' is reproduced through the filter's own domain read out of the search view (asserted to be [('active','=',True)], and asserted to be switched on by the action's search_default_connected) rather than retyped, and the resulting population is checked for the two shapes that need no baseline: a '%(Template)' row leaking past the action's domain, and two store rows sharing a name (the same store migrated twice would import every order twice). Step 6's substance — 'the card and the list agree' — is asserted on the record and on what each view binds. See _finding_card_readings for why step 5 cannot be performed as written.
TC-CHN-005.expected_verdict: PASSED on the v19 restore, with the card-readings finding logged. last_sync_order reads 2026-08-10 02:04:00 — non-blank and not today — and exactly one Shopify store is listed.
residual_manual: Compare Status and Last Order Sync against the Novobi baseline read at the upgrade cut-off; both are in TC-CHN-005-sync-state.csv with a blank Baseline column.
Confirm against the printout that the rows in TC-CHN-005-stores-listed.csv are the stores that should exist — only the baseline says which disconnected stores were expected to come across.
Read Last Order Sync off the Manage Stores LIST, not the Overview card, on this build.

TC-CHN-011.reason: GATE 6's discrimination, done properly. The figures are read from the card's own producer (get_dashboard_datas, a public method whose return value the kanban_dashboard compute just json.dumps) and then recomputed independently over sale.order, which is the only way to tell 'the figure is zero because there are no orders' from 'the figure is zero because the screen is reading the wrong place'. Two things make the naive version of that comparison wrong and are handled: multichannel_order overrides get_dashboard_datas WITHOUT super() (multichannel_order/models/ecommerce_channel.py:212-223 over omni_manage_channel/...:534), so on a full install the payload keys are total_sales / num_of_orders / num_of_unshipped_orders / lead_time and not the base module's sales_total / sales_unit — a test asserting on the latter would KeyError; and the window is NOT fixed at 30 days, it comes from the store's own kanban_dashboard_period through KANBAN_DASHBOARD_PERIOD_MAPPING (:20-25, 228-229), so a test assuming 30 would pass by luck. The recomputation reproduces the query's own boundary expression and its state='sale'-only term (whose inline BC-016 note records that 'done' is not a v19 sale-order state). Step 9 is done three ways and all three are reported: the card's exact domain, the same window through read_group by Store (the workbook's own group-by), and the same window with the state facet cleared — the last because on this database that gives 5 rather than 0 and a tester who clears the default facet would file a false GATE-6 defect. The suite also records that there is NO 'last 30 days' filter on the Sales search view (core offers only month/quarter/year on Order Date), so the workbook's step 9 is under-specified and needs an explicit custom range. The graph is asserted at payload level: labels present, at least one series, and every series carrying one value per label — and the field the card reads is asserted to carry the same payload the method returns. The three-dot menu's View/Action/Log sections are asserted to exist with their workbook labels and with at least one entry each. See _finding_card_readings and _finding_period_write for the two divergences.
TC-CHN-011.expected_verdict: PASSED on the v19 restore, taking the zero branch: 0 confirmed channel orders fall in the current 30-day window (the newest is dated 2026-08-07), so the figures legitimately read zero, GATE 6's 'zeroes while real orders exist' is asserted false, and the figure checks are marked N/A with the reason — which is what the workbook's own precondition instructs. The 90-day window holds 180 orders / 120,996.30, so 'the period selector changes the figures' is demonstrated.
residual_manual: The one click the workbook asks for — switching the period selector on the card from Last 30 days to Last 90 days — is not automated; see _finding_period_write. Do it by hand, compare against TC-CHN-011-period-windows.csv, and set it back to Last 30 days as the State After The Test column says.
Mark the figure checks N/A with the reason while no confirmed store order falls in the selected period; the newest confirmed order is named in the log.
The OWL render itself is not asserted here (no browser); see _no_browser.

_finding_salesperson.workbook_line: Expected Result line 4 — 'Salesperson is present on the Order Configuration tab and carries the expected user. (Novobi restored this field during the upgrade; it was missing from the screen in an earlier build.)'
_finding_salesperson.finding: Half of that is true. ecommerce.channel.user_id (string 'Salesperson') WAS restored on the model, deliberately and with a note, under FG11-D2 / BC-012 (multichannel_order/models/ecommerce_channel.py:44-61) — including a BC-029 fix to its domain, because v19 renamed res.users.groups_id to group_ids. But it was restored on the MODEL ONLY: there is no <field name="user_id"/> in any ecommerce.channel view on staging_19, where v15 carried one on exactly the tab the workbook names (novobi-omni-addons/multichannel_order/views/omnichannel_dashboard_views.xml:71, inside <group name="top_left"> of <page name="order_configuration_page">). So the field is not on the Order Configuration tab, cannot be read or set from the screen, and on the MMG restore it is empty.
_finding_salesperson.handling: Asserted as written. AUTOMATION_CONVENTIONS rule 2 makes this an assertion, not a note, so TEST-FG08-CHN-001 FAILS on the shipped build and the log names both source locations. The fix is a one-line view addition.
_finding_salesperson.severity: P0 — the workbook names this field explicitly and TC-ORD-015 depends on it for channel revenue attribution.

_finding_card_readings.case: TC-CHN-005 step 5, TC-CHN-011 steps 4-5 and Expected Result line 2
_finding_card_readings.workbook_line: TC-CHN-005 step 5 — 'read the same two values off the store's card, plus the Total sales and Total orders tiles'. TC-CHN-011 step 4 — 'Read the Last order sync value'; step 5 — 'Read Total sales last 30 days and Total orders last 30 days'.
_finding_card_readings.finding: None of those three readings is on the v19 card. The base kanban card carried a col-md-9 block holding 'Last order sync', 'Total sales last 30 days' and 'Total orders last 30 days' (omni_manage_channel/views/omnichannel_dashboard_views.xml:61-88); multichannel_order REPLACES that whole block with the period selector (multichannel_order/views/omnichannel_dashboard_views.xml:8-14). The col-md-3 sibling holding the connection badge survives, so Status IS still on the card. The removal is internally consistent rather than accidental: the same module newly overrides get_dashboard_datas() without super() (…/models/ecommerce_channel.py:212-223), so the sales_total / sales_unit keys those two tiles read (omni_manage_channel/models/ecommerce_channel.py:568-571) are no longer in the payload either. On v15 NEITHER had happened — novobi-omni-addons/multichannel_order/views/omnichannel_dashboard_views.xml:8-16 only ADDED the graph, and get_dashboard_datas existed only in omni_manage_channel.
_finding_card_readings.handling: Recorded as a WORKBOOK AMENDMENT item and asserted in neither direction, following the FG-06 TC-DEP-013 precedent. No migrated value is wrong, and the workbook itself says the rebuilt items must not be reported as unexpected. The substance is asserted on the v19 equivalents — the Store Statistics panel's Total Sales and # Orders over the selected period (multichannel_order/views/omnichannel_dashboard_views.xml:27-52) — and the tester is redirected to read Last Order Sync off the Manage Stores list.
_finding_card_readings.severity: Workbook amendment. Steps TC-CHN-005/5, TC-CHN-011/4 and TC-CHN-011/5 need rewriting against the rebuilt screen.

_finding_period_write.workbook_line: 'Find the period selector on the card and change it from Last 30 days to Last 90 days. Confirm the figures change.' State After The Test: 'The period selector may be left on whatever you last chose. Set it back to Last 30 days.'
_finding_period_write.finding: The selector is a STORED field, kanban_dashboard_period, edited in place on the card (widget='kanban_editable_selection_field' force_save='1', multichannel_order/views/omnichannel_dashboard_views.xml:11). Changing it is a write() on the live store record. AUTOMATION_CONVENTIONS rule 3 forbids modifying a pre-existing business record, and for a shopify channel write() routes through ShopifyChannel.write, which calls extract_shopify_store_settings — an outbound shopify_get_store_settings call — whenever either credential field is in vals (multichannel_shopify/models/ecommerce_channel.py:427-435, 445-451). The workbook authorises the click for a human; the platform does not take that authorisation for itself.
_finding_period_write.handling: The expectation is proved read-only and more thoroughly than the manual step: the selector's four options are asserted from fields_get, its binding on the card from the arch, its wiring to the window from the mapping constant, and the figures are recomputed for ALL FOUR windows to show they genuinely differ — with the same GATE-6 discrimination applied when two windows agree. The one click is recorded as a RESIDUAL MANUAL STEP with this reason, and the final step asserts the field is unchanged so the workbook's 'set it back' has nothing to undo.
_finding_period_write.severity: Deliberate automation limit, disclosed. Not a product defect.

_verification_before_delivery: No Odoo server was running when this suite was written and none was started against the v19 restore, because loading Odoo against that database risks a registry update and a cron firing at an ACTIVE store with auto_import_data on. Verification was therefore done offline against mmg_19 over read-only PostgreSQL: (1) every XML id the suite references resolves (15 of 15: the four menus, both actions, four views, three groups, sale.action_orders); (2) every field it reads exists — 80 STORE_FIELDS, all 36 WORKBOOK_FIELDS, all 18 ROUTING_M2O fields and their comodels — and the four deliberately dropped v15 fields are confirmed absent; (3) the menu parentage and group restriction the suite asserts match the database (Manage Stores parent = Store Configuration, group_ids = [E-commerce Manager]); (4) the arch parsers were run over the real ir_ui_view.arch_db of all eleven ecommerce.channel views, and every (tab, field) pair in the suite's mapping table resolves to the right page — including the five that multichannel_shopify places through xpaths into groups other modules own — with user_id the single field on no page, which is the finding; (5) the list columns, the Connected filter's domain and the three-dot section labels match the assertions verbatim; (6) number_from() was unit-tested over 20 cases covering the real output of thousand_repr / readable_repr / currency_repr, which caught and fixed a separator bug that would have parsed '$ 120,996' as 120.996. What remains unverified until first run: the shape of a handful of RPC return values (read_group's count key is handled both ways) and the assembled-arch assertions, which need a live get_view.
